rare_regions.activation_trigger: Asynchronous reset asserted (rst_n deasserted / low) at power-up or reset event
rare_regions.description: Reset branch in the baud-rate generator always_ff block. This initialization path executes only when the asynchronous reset is asserted (rare during normal running operation).
rare_regions.matched_line_content: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

rare_regions.activation_trigger: Asynchronous reset asserted (rst_n deasserted / low) to initialize state machine to IDLE
rare_regions.description: State register initialization on reset. The 'if (!rst_n)' branch runs only on reset, making this a rare execution region compared to normal state transitions.
rare_regions.matched_line_content: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin

rare_regions.activation_trigger: Encountering an undefined/invalid state value (state not matched by IDLE/START_BIT/DATA_BITS/STOP_BIT)
rare_regions.description: Default recovery in the combinational state transition logic. This path is intended to recover from invalid states — an uncommon event during correct operation, thus a rare region.

rare_regions.activation_trigger: `FORMAL` define enabled (formal verification build); assertions exercised during formal checks, not in normal synthesis or runtime
rare_regions.description: Assertions wrapped in `ifdef FORMAL` are only active during formal verification runs. They represent verification-only checks and are not executed in typical hardware operation — a distinctly rare/conditional execution domain.

rare_regions.activation_trigger: Simulation reset assertion/deassertion and explicit test stimulus sequence (initial block executed at simulation start)
rare_regions.description: This initial block performs reset (rst_n asserted then deasserted), drives two transmit transactions, waits for tx_ready, and calls $finish. Reset and end-of-simulation behavior are initialization/termination events and the specific wait-for-ready paths are only exercised during the test — making this a rare/one-shot execution region in the context of continuous hardware operation.

rare_regions.activation_trigger: Waiting for DUT to assert tx_ready before continuing (synchronization point in test stimulus)
rare_regions.description: The `wait(tx_ready);` statements (used twice in the stimulus block) cause the testbench to pause until the DUT signals readiness. In hardware these synchronization points represent rare/uncommon timing conditions (especially if the DUT stalls or deadlocks), and are only executed during the specific test sequence.

rare_regions.rare_region_code:
initial begin
        $monitor("Time=%0t rst_n=%b tx_data=%h tx_valid=%b tx_ready=%b tx_out=%b", 
                 $time, rst_n, tx_data, tx_valid, tx_ready, tx_out);
    end
rare_regions.activation_trigger: Simulation start (initial block enabling runtime monitoring/logging)
rare_regions.description: $monitor is a simulation-only observation/debug facility. It runs only under simulation and is not synthesizable — making it a rare/diagnostic execution region compared with normal synthesized logic.
